messages:
marta: Heads-up — the access-review automation flagged ~120 grants this morning. Most are bot svcaccts, but I spotted a few unexpected cross-project KMS bindings. Anyone own `billing-liaison-svc`? :eyes:
kevin: I took a quick look. Two bindings show `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for a service account from a different project. Looks like an infra deploy step accidentally used the wrong principal. Snippet from our permission export:
```json
[{
  "principal": "serviceAccount:billing-liaison-svc@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "binding": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter",
  "resource": "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/billing/cryptoKeys/enc"
}]
```
samir: Ugh. Our automation matcher currently flags any wildcard-ish resource combos. We should add an allowlist for service accounts with `provisioner:infra` tag or `approved_by:security` label so we don't get noisy alerts. Also, we need to treat KMS bindings specially — they require correlation with audit logs before remediation.
olivia: Agreed. To verify activity, run a short KMS audit query: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"billing-liaison-svc@*"' --limit 50` — that'll show if the svcacct actually used the key recently.
marta: Can someone run that and paste the top lines here? If it's unused, I'd like to revoke the binding and open a small incident PR documenting the change and the rollback plan. :lock:
kevin: Ran it — only 3 Encrypt entries across the last 30 days, all from a CI runner that was misconfigured. I revoked the binding in the project and added a temporary tag `revoked_by:eng-security`. Steps I took:
- Removed IAM binding: `gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member='serviceAccount:billing-liaison-svc@...' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'`
- Recorded the change in the infra audit doc (link pasted)
- Notified the infra team to fix the CI principal
jamie: FYI I filed a short incident note and linked the PR for the revocation + remediation instructions. infra-bot: permissions-scan completed — 0 outstanding critical KMS bindings. :white_check_mark:
marta: Thanks all. Two action items: 1) include this as an example in the quarterly access-review deck (how KMS bindings differ), 2) adjust automation to filter approved provisioner tags before creating noisy tickets. I'll draft the deck blurb and a PR template for exceptions.
kevin: I'll add a unit to the automation to consult the entitlement export for `approved_by` labels and to run the KMS audit query before escalating. Quick pseudo: `if is_kms_binding and not approved_tag: run_kms_audit_and_hold()`
samir: Also propose adding a short TTL policy for cross-project KMS grants — auto-expire after 7 days unless validated. We can include that as a mitigation in the runbook.
marta: Perfect. I'll follow up with a tiny runbook patch and a checklist for oncall to run if automation holds a KMS finding. Closing the thread once PRs are up. :thumbsup:
